Stacked on #5086 (probe-first open); only the top commit is new here.
Review that one first.

## What

`bd init --proxied-server` remains the only command whose open may
create the database. Normal command opens of a missing database now fail
with `database "<name>" not found on Dolt server; run 'bd init' to
create it` instead of silently creating one.

## Why

Follows #2189's principle: do not create a database unless explicitly
initializing one. Stacked on #5086, which supplies the mechanism
(`WithCreateIfMissing`, default true) and its tests; this PR is the
cmd/bd policy wiring only, passing the option explicitly at every
proxied provider call site. Together they close the create half of
#5079.

## Verification

- Storage-layer behavior (guard error, nothing created) is tested in
  #5086
  (`-run TestNewExternalDoltServerUOWProvider_MissingDatabaseWithCreateDisabled`).
- `make ci-pr-lint`, `make ci-pr-policy`, `make ci-pr-core` pass locally
  on the stack.
- End-to-end: `bd init --proxied-server` creates the database; after
  dropping it server-side, the next `bd list` fails with the not-found
  error and creates nothing.
- Existing proxied init/end-to-end tests pass unchanged.

Note: open PR #4303 touches cmd/bd/uow_factory.go (constructor
signatures most likely to conflict); functionally independent, and I am
happy to rebase whichever lands second.

381 pr5085.diff
## What

Embedded federation sync now uses the credentials stored by
`bd federation add-peer`, falling back to the
`DOLT_REMOTE_USER`/`DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD` environment pair when a remote
has no stored credentials.

## Why

add-peer promises "credentials are encrypted and stored locally. They
are used automatically when syncing with the peer", but embedded sync
read only the environment, so first sync against any authenticated Dolt
server presented the wrong identity (#5080). This is the peer-path
remainder of the class fixed for default remotes in #2543.

Resolution order is peer store first, environment second, and unknown
remotes are untouched: federation sync iterates every dolt remote, so
plain remotes and credential-free peers keep their current behavior.

On concurrency: the in-process Dolt engine reads these variables from
the process environment, so a stored pair is exported only inside a
`federationEnvMutex` critical section and both variables are restored
afterward, including when the operation fails; a stored empty field
unsets its variable rather than inheriting an ambient value. Stored-peer
operations are therefore serialized against each other. Operations with
no stored credentials read the environment without the lock, matching
the existing server-mode semantics (`withRemoteOperationEnv` locks only
when credentials are present).

Fixes #5080.

Thanks for this pair — the stack split is exactly right (mechanism in #5086, policy here), the probe-first design with the bare-CREATE arbitration preserved is careful work, and the wildcard-safe `DatabaseExists` iteration with the comment explaining *why* `SHOW DATABASES LIKE` is unsafe is the kind of detail we love to see. The least-privilege regression test is a faithful repro of #5079. We want to land this stack, and ahead of #4303 to keep your rebase burden low.

Four asks before we do — three small, one design question:

1. **Point existing projects at `bd bootstrap`, not `bd init`.** The not-found error (`internal/storage/uow/dolt_sql_provider.go`, the `!createIfMissing` branch) says `run 'bd init' to create it`. The common way to hit this path is a machine that just cloned an existing project (or whose configured DB was dropped server-side) — for those, `bd init` is the wrong tool and can steer people into re-initializing a workspace that should be bootstrapped from the remote. Suggest wording like: `run 'bd init' to create a new database, or 'bd bootstrap' to restore an existing project`.

2. **`createIfMissing` defaulting to `true` re-opens the hole for future callers.** Every current call site passes the option explicitly, which is great — but the default in `newUOWProviderOptions` means the next caller of `NewExternalDoltServerUOWProvider`/`NewDoltServerUOWProvider` who forgets the option silently gets the implicit-create behavior this PR exists to remove. Since you already touched every call site, flipping the default to `false` (init passes `WithCreateIfMissing(true)` explicitly) makes the safe behavior the one you get by accident. If there is an external/embedder compat reason to keep `true`, a comment at the default saying so would do.

3. **The cmd/bd policy wiring has no test.** Both new tests exercise the storage layer via Docker (`StartIsolatedDoltContainer`), but nothing asserts the actual policy this PR adds: `bd init` opens with create enabled and every other command path (root command, `dolt clean-databases`) opens with create disabled. A lightweight non-Docker test — even just asserting which option `newProxiedServerUOWProvider` receives from each call site, or a fake-provider seam — would keep the wiring from regressing when #4303 reshapes `uow_factory.go` constructor signatures. That collision is likely, so a guard here is cheap insurance.

4. **Design question: should `bd dolt clean-databases` require the configured DB to exist?** `runDoltCleanDatabasesProxied` now passes `WithCreateIfMissing(false)`, so if the configured database was dropped server-side, the cleanup command fails at open with not-found. But cleaning up stale databases is precisely what you might reach for in that broken state. Should it open without binding to the configured database (probe-only / no `USE`), or is failing fast the intended behavior here? Either answer is fine — we would just like it to be deliberate, and a line in the PR body or a comment covering it.

Happy to help with any of these if you would rather we push follow-ups — say the word. Once these are settled we plan to land #5087 as the two-commit stack and close #5086 as carried-by-stack with attribution.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Measure contributor waiting queue for gastownhall/beads open PRs.
# Output TSV: pr, author, class, days_waiting, last_maintainer_event, last_contributor_event
set -u
REPO=gastownhall/beads
MAINTAINERS='maphew|steveyegge'
now=$(date -u +%s)
out="$1"
: > "$out"
prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --state open --limit 200 --json number,author,isDraft \
  --jq '.[] | select(.isDraft|not) | select(.author.is_bot|not) | select(.author.login|test("'"$MAINTAINERS"'")|not) | "\(.number)\t\(.author.login)"')
total=$(wc -l <<<"$prs")
echo "# measured_at=$(date -u +%FT%TZ) eligible=$total" >> "$out"
while IFS=$'\t' read -r pr author; do
  [ -z "$pr" ] && continue
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    json=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$REPO" --json comments,reviews,updatedAt 2>/dev/null) && break
    sleep 2
  done
  [ -z "${json:-}" ] && { echo -e "$pr\t$author\tERROR\t-\t-\t-" >> "$out"; continue; }
  last_maint=$(jq -r --arg m "$MAINTAINERS" '
    [ (.comments[]? | {t:.createdAt, w:.author.login}),
      (.reviews[]?  | {t:(.submittedAt // .createdAt), w:.author.login}) ]
    | map(select(.w != null and (.w|test($m)))) | sort_by(.t) | last | .t // empty' <<<"$json")
  last_contrib=$(jq -r --arg m "$MAINTAINERS" --arg a "$author" '
    [ (.comments[]? | {t:.createdAt, w:.author.login}),
      (.reviews[]?  | {t:(.submittedAt // .createdAt), w:.author.login}) ]
    | map(select(.w != null and ((.w|test($m))|not))) | sort_by(.t) | last | .t // empty' <<<"$json")
  if [ -z "$last_maint" ]; then
    cls=NEVER_ANSWERED
    ref=$last_contrib
  elif [ -n "$last_contrib" ] && [[ "$last_contrib" > "$last_maint" ]]; then
    cls=WAITING_AGAIN
    ref=$last_contrib
  else
    cls=ANSWERED
    ref=$last_maint
  fi
  days='-'
  if [ -n "${ref:-}" ]; then
    rs=$(date -u -d "$ref" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    [ -n "$rs" ] && days=$(( (now - rs) / 86400 ))
  fi
  echo -e "$pr\t$author\t$cls\t$days\t${last_maint:--}\t${last_contrib:--}" >> "$out"
done <<< "$prs"
echo "# done" >> "$out"

input.content:
Thank you for closing the add-peer promise gap — this is careful concurrency work and it shows. We verified the parts that worried us and they hold: the defer ordering in `withPeerAuth` registers `Unlock` before the restore closure, so LIFO restores the environment *before* releasing the mutex (and on panic); `overrideEnv`'s `os.LookupEnv` restores "was unset" as unset rather than `""`; and the empty-field-unsets rule is actually stricter than the cleanup in package `dolt`'s own `setFederationCredentials`, which unconditionally `Unsetenv`s and clobbers pre-existing ambient values — your `overrideEnv` shape is the fix that package wants too, if you ever feel like a follow-up there. The `errors.Is(..., ErrNotFound)` chain survives the `errors.Join` wrapping, and the unknown-remote fallback test pins it. Approving as a strict improvement over env-only.

Four follow-ups we would love to see — the first two matter, and we are happy to take any of them maintainer-side if you would rather stop here:

1. **The same bug survives in `bd sync --remote <peer>` and `bd dolt push|pull --remote <peer>`.** A federation peer is registered as an ordinary Dolt remote under the same name (`AddRemoteIfNotExists(peer.Name, ...)`), and `PushRemote`/`PullRemote` in `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/version_control.go` still read only `remoteAuthUser()`. So after this PR, `bd federation sync --peer team` presents stored credentials while `bd sync --remote team` still presents the env identity — the #5080 failure via a different verb. Routing those two through `withPeerAuth` closes it, and the `ErrNotFound` fallback makes it a no-op for plain remotes. It would also close the residual unsynchronized-env-reader window (`remoteAuthUser` call sites read env without the lock while the in-process engine does the same), which today is only reachable by embedders and parallel tests, but is free to fix with the same edit.

2. **Undecryptable stored credentials now hard-fail with a raw cipher error.** `federation_peers` rows replicate with the database, but `.beads-credential-key` is machine-local and gitignored — so machine B pulls the DB, silently generates its own key, and every peer sync dies with `resolve peer credentials: decrypt password: cipher: message authentication failed` (and `bd federation status` renders it as `Unreachable:`, pointing at the network instead of the local key). Hard-fail is a defensible choice — server mode already behaves this way, and silently falling back could present the wrong identity — but the error should say what actually happened and what to do: that the credential key is machine-local, and to re-run `bd federation add-peer <name> <url> --user ...`. Whatever semantics you settle on, a test pinning the decrypt-failure branch would keep it from being changed by accident later.

3. Two comment nits: `federationEnvMutex` here is a *separate* lock from package `dolt`'s mutex of the same name — the "mirroring package dolt's federationEnvMutex" comment reads like it is the same lock, and one clause ("a separate lock; the two stores never run remote ops concurrently") would prevent the misread. Similarly, the PR-body claim that lock-free env reads "match the existing server-mode semantics" is not quite equivalent: server mode's lock-free branch talks to an external server that cannot see this process's env, while embedded mode's genuinely reads env for the in-process engine.

4. Diagnostic nit: a peer saved with a username but an empty password (Enter at the interactive prompt) now deliberately suppresses an ambient `DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD` — correct as a security default, but a user whose pre-PR setup worked off the env gets an auth failure with no hint. A one-line stderr/debug warning when a peer has a username, no stored password, and `DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD` set would save them the puzzle.

One mechanical thing before merge: the three CI failures on this run (`errcheck` on `windows.CloseHandle` in `internal/procid` and `internal/storage/dbproxy`) are inherited from the branch point — current main already fixes them, and your branch is ~50 commits behind. A rebase onto main should take CI green without touching your change.

This round closes it out — approving. You addressed all four items from the last review in one clean rebase, corrected the mechanism argument instead of hand-waving it, and pulled the repro harness when it turned out to be a false green. That last one is the kind of intellectual honesty that makes reviews easy, and it is appreciated.

We re-verified independently before approving: the patch applies clean to current main (all 8 `CALL DOLT_*` sites in `internal/storage/schema/` unmoved, and the diff converts all 8 — `unstageIgnoredTables` delegates to a converted site, so there is no ninth); the driver claim holds in the pinned source (`mysqlConn.exec` has three early error returns before its terminal `discardResults`, while `mysqlRows.Close` drains unconditionally — Exec-on-error dirties the wire, Query+Close does not); the drain loop plus deferred Close covers multi-result-set procedures on both the clean and mid-stream-error paths; and `drainCall` with args stays on the server-side prepared path exactly as `ExecContext` did, so no protocol change. On part B, the `repairKey` registry is a behavior-preserving refactor of main's switch (no competing repair has landed since), `--skip-empty` and the `dolt_nonlocal_tables` column list check out against the pinned Dolt, and the by-name staging correctly keeps the bounded-migrate working set out of repair-labeled commits.

Three follow-ups, none blocking — say the word if you would rather we take any of them maintainer-side after the merge:

1. `migration_body_drain_test.go` — the guard test's ground truth is `strings.Contains(upper, "CALL DOLT_COMMIT")` while `procedureCallRe` matches any `CALL`. A future migration using only `CALL DOLT_ADD`/`DOLT_RESET` trips the `detected && !hasCall` branch and fails CI for doing the correct thing. One-line fix: ground truth `"CALL DOLT_"`.
2. `repairPartial0041NonlocalDelete` cannot distinguish "0041 died right after its leading DELETE+COMMIT" from "0041 died after the `depends_on_wisp_id` ALTER" — in the second case the replay's `@needs_migrate` guard then skips the remaining body and records v41 over a `dependencies` table with no rebuilt PK/FK/indexes, where pre-patch that state hard-failed visibly. The window is narrow (per-step commits leave those ALTERs as uncommitted changes the dirty guard catches first), so either a comment saying exactly that, or an additional gate on `depends_on_wisp_id` being absent, would do.
3. `commitNonlocalRepair`'s `CALL DOLT_ADD('dolt_nonlocal_tables')` is not tolerant of Dolt's "table not in working set" error, so on an engine where nonlocal mutations never enter the working root it converts a `nothing to commit` failure into a differently-worded staging failure. One line: tolerate the no-op the way `commitMigrationStep` tolerates `nothing to commit`.

Two nits at your discretion: `drainCall` drops the deferred `rows.Close()` error (a drain failure inside Close returns nil while the conn is still dirty — the exact class the function exists to prevent; `defer func() { err = errors.Join(err, rows.Close()) }()` closes it), and the comment-only `t.Cleanup` body in `initschema_idempotent_test.go` can go.

One small ask before merge: the PR description is now stale — it still describes editing 0040 to `INSERT IGNORE` and adding `--skip-empty` to the shipped migration bytes, which the final diff deliberately does not do (frozen bytes stay frozen; repairs live in the registry). Since the squash commit message inherits from the description, a quick refresh keeps the history honest.

For the record on scope: this does not close gastownhall/beads#4800 — on a pristine store both repairs correctly short-circuit before touching anything, and #4800's frozen-`DOLT_COMMIT`-finds-no-diff failure is a different mechanism. We will note that there so the correlation doesn't auto-retire it.

We also spotted that the same undrained-CALL shape exists at much higher call volume on transaction-pinned connections in `internal/storage/dolt/` (`issues.go`, `slots.go`, `store.go` — `_, _ = tx.ExecContext("CALL DOLT_ADD...")` followed by `CALL DOLT_COMMIT` on the same tx). That is out of scope here and tracked on our side; mentioning it in case you want first crack at it, since it is your pattern.

Merge mechanics: our patrol lands this once the base branch is green again (a flake-rerun is settling on main right now). Thanks for the persistence across three rounds — this is a genuinely valuable fix.

`bd dep add <a> <b> --type blocked-by` silently creates a **semantically inert** dependency: it is stored, displayed by `bd show`, and reported with a success message, but it does not gate `bd ready` / `bd blocked`.

The same token works correctly on the *other* path — `bd create --deps blocked-by:<id>` maps it to `blocks`.

This bites because **`blocked-by` is the exact word `bd dep add --help` uses** for the blocking relationship:

> The `--blocked-by` and `--depends-on` flags are aliases and both mean "issue-123 depends on (is blocked by) the specified issue."

So the most natural value to pass to `--type`, taken verbatim from the command's own help text, produces an edge that looks right everywhere you inspect it and enforces nothing.

## Reproduction

Observed with **bd 1.1.0 (`3fea70523`, `main@3fea70523a5b`)**.

```
# inert — stored as the literal custom type "blocked-by"
bd dep add ISSUE-A ISSUE-B --type blocked-by
bd show ISSUE-A --json     # -> dependency_type: "blocked-by"
bd ready                   # -> ISSUE-A IS STILL LISTED
bd blocked                 # -> ISSUE-A is ABSENT

# correct — stored as "blocks"
bd dep add ISSUE-A ISSUE-B
bd show ISSUE-A --json  
comments: 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tri-submit — finalize a PR review: post the DISTILLED post file to upstream
# as a gh pr review with the chosen verdict, then close the bd issue and apply
# the upstream 'triaged' label (via tri-close).
#
# Two files, two audiences:
#   _working_on/pr-reviews/NNNN.md       full analysis — stays local, never posted
#   _working_on/pr-reviews/NNNN.post.md  distilled post — the ONLY body posted
#
# The post file must fit the word budget (default 150 words, fenced code
# excluded; TRI_POST_MAX_WORDS or --max-words to override deliberately), and
# posting requires interactive confirmation at a terminal — unattended agents
# cannot post text upstream.
#
# Usage:
#   tri-submit <bd-id-or-pr-num> --approve
#   tri-submit <id> --request-changes
#   tri-submit <id> --comment
#   tri-submit <id> --approve --dry-run     # show what would be posted
#   tri-submit <id> --comment --max-words 250
#
# Requires the review note (NNNN.md) to exist with its 'Verdict' line filled
# in, and the post file (NNNN.post.md) to be distilled from it.

<result>## Verdict on the three claimed blocker fixes

All three were re-verified against PR head `d484d2e7b` (fetched locally as branch `pr4844-review` in `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main`; CI on that head is 77/77 green and the three new embedded tests demonstrably ran and passed — `TestEmbeddedRebaseRemoteDominates` 10.23s, `...WispSubtree` 10.48s, `...LocalDominates` 10.65s in job 89759665405).

### 1. Wisp-aware subtree enumeration — HOLDS (for the defect as filed)

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:316-353` (`subtreeIDs` / `subtreeIDsFromTable`) enumerates both `issues` and `wisps`, degrading cleanly on `dberrors.IsTableNotExist`. `renameSubtreeInTx` (:354-388) picks the source table per id via `issueops.IsActiveWispInTx` before loading the row, so a wisp child of a durable root no longer aborts the rename with `sql: no rows`.

The test genuinely exercises it: `rebase_collision_test.go` inserts `p+".71.1"` into `wisps` under durable local `.71`, then asserts `wispExists(p+".71.1") == false` and `wispTitleOf(p+".74.1") == "WispChild"`. Without the fix the wisp stays at `.71.1` and the first assertion fails. Confirmed real.

### 2. Abort parity (`hadViol && !repairedViol`) — HOLDS

`rebase.go:493-506` is a faithful mirror of `mergesettle.go:132-146`: `TryRepairFKCascadeViolations` result is now captured, `violErr != nil` aborts, and `hadViol && !repairedViol` aborts with an explicit error rather than relying on `DOLT_COMMIT`'s gate (which `dolt_force_transaction_commit=1` defeats). The added `GetConflicts` check at :481-492 is actually *stricter* than `SettleMerge`, which only re-checks conflicts when `!resolved`. No parity gap found.

Session-flag hygiene is fine in both callers: `withPinnedDBConn` opens and closes a fresh `*sql.DB` per call (`embeddeddolt/version_control.go:53-78`), and `openLongTimeoutConn` likewise (`dolt/store.go:3353-3365`), so the two `SET @@dolt_*` flags cannot leak back into the shared pool.

### 3. Atomicity (hard-reset-to-backup-tag on any failure) — HOLDS, with two gaps

Every `return` after the tag is created (`rebase.go:121-130` defer, registered immediately after `report.BackupTag = backupTag` at :112) assigns the named `retErr`, so the reset fires on: `renumberCollisions` error (:139), renumber `DOLT_COMMIT` error (:144), `mergeAndSettleRebase` error (:152), `swapRenumberedSubtrees` error (:161), and the local-dominates commit (:166). Traced all of them; none escapes.

I also confirmed the reset is *not* destructive to session wisps, contrary to what the PR's own comment at `rebase.go:132-135` implies. Dolt's `resetHardTables` calls `MoveUntrackedTables(working, staged, head)` (`.../dolt/go@v0.40.5-.../libraries/doltcore/env/actions/reset.go:65-75`), which carries tables present in working-but-not-staged onto the target root. `wisps`/`wisp_*` are `dolt_ignore`d and never staged, so they survive `DOLT_RESET('--hard', tag)`. The design choice (stay on the local branch) is still right, but the stated justification is inaccurate — worth correcting so a future reader doesn't "fix" it the wrong way.

Two residual gaps, both should-fix:

- **Panic bypasses the restore.** `rebase.go:122-124` returns early when `retErr == nil`, which is exactly the state during a panic unwind. A panic between the renumber `DOLT_COMMIT` (:143) and the merge leaves a stranded renumber commit. Add `if r := recover(); r != nil { reset; panic(r) }`.
- **Context cancellation defeats the restore.** The reset reuses the caller's `ctx` (`rebase.go:125`). A Ctrl-C / deadline that killed the merge also kills the reset, producing the "automatic restore also failed" branch and stranded commits. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (plus a short timeout) for the restore statement.

## New / still-open correctness findings

### A. `maxChildNumber` ignores `child_counters` and `wisps` — blocker

`rebase.go:422-441`. The doc comment claims it "Mirrors the child-scan in `issueops.GetNextChildIDTx`", but `GetNextChildIDTx` (`internal/storage/issueops/child_id.go:15-50`) *seeds* from `last_child` in the counter table and only then takes the max with the id scan. The PR drops the counter half and scans `issues` only. Two concrete failures:

1. **Reuse of an already-issued, deleted id.** `bd delete` never lowers `child_counters.last_child`. Parent `P` with `child_counters=73` after `P.73` was created and deleted; `issues` max is 72. `renumberCollisions` seeds `next[P]=72` (`rebase.go:250-263`) and mints `P.73` — an id another clone may still hold. fix(create): hard-fail multi-type same-target --deps (#4626)
## Summary

`bd create --deps 'discovered-from:X,blocked-by:X'` could silently keep only one edge: dependency uniqueness is per `(issue_id, target)` (`uk_dep_issue_target`), not per type, and `AddDependency` failures were only warned.

This change:

1. Expands comma-separated `--deps` tokens and parses via `parseDepSpecs`
2. Rejects multi-type / duplicate edges that would collide on the same target **before** create
3. Hard-fails create if `AddDependency` errors (no silent partial apply)

Schema
+++ b/cmd/bd/create.go
+++ b/cmd/bd/create_deps.go
+++ b/cmd/bd/create_deps_atomic_test.go
+++ b/cmd/bd/create_deps_test.go
+++ b/cmd/bd/create_proxied_server.go

## What

`bd dep add A B --type blocked-by` (and `--type depends-on`, via the single-edge, bulk `--file`, and proxied-server code paths) now normalizes to the canonical `blocks` storage type, through shared `canonicalDependencyType()`/`validateDependencyType()` helpers extracted from `bd create --deps`'s existing alias handling. `dep add --type` also now rejects unknown/custom dependency types, matching `create --deps`'s existing behavior, and its output reports the stored canonical type rather than echoing the raw flag value.

## Why

`--type blocked-by` — the exact word `bd dep add --help` itself uses to describe the blocking relationship — silently stored the literal string `blocked-by`. The edge displayed correctly everywhere (`dep list`, `dep tree`, `show`), but never gated `bd ready`/`bd blocked`, which check the canonical type constants. An edge that looks right everywhere you inspect it and enforces nothing is worse than an error; it bit our own coordination tracker twice this week before we traced it.

The `--type` path simply lacked the alias mapping that `create --deps` already had; this consolidates both paths onto one implementation so they cannot drift again. The design intent documented on `types.WellKnownDependencyTypes()` ("accepted by user-facing commands that intentionally reject custom dependency types") already reads as plural — `dep add` was the straggler.

Fixes #5069.

- New table tests `TestCanonicalDependencyType` / `TestValidateDependencyType`; existing `TestParseDepSpecs` and dep-suite tests all pass.

## Why

This ports the fix from #5042 (merged) — which closed the same hole for the proxied/uow path — to the server-mode path, the remaining half of the #5012 family. Without it, a session dying between a migration step's SQL and its per-step Dolt commit leaves debris that the next retry's `MigrateUp` misclassifies as pre-existing dirty user data (`*DirtyTablesError`), which the retry loop treats as permanent — unconvergeable on a database that didn't exist seconds earlier.

One structural difference is intentionally not ported: uow re-issues `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` on every retry attempt because creation and migration share one retry loop there. Server mode creates the database exactly once, before the migration retry loop starts, so `createdDatabase` is a fixed invariant for the whole retry sequence.
